terms: AI Features;AI Features Addendum;Ecommerce AI;Conversational shopping
reading: core: Commerce's own AI Features, which it may suspend, modify or discontinue (BC-S-0351), under an AI Features Addendum (BC-I-0473). outside, a reading: Commerce's third-party providers are used to provide the AI Features (BC-S-0353); the statement names no provider. extension-point: the App Marketplace has a category Ecommerce AI (BC-I-0477). The customer remains responsible for Third-Party Products that enable AI (BC-S-0352): shows. The product line Conversational shopping (BC-I-0516) is named only; whether it serves the merchant or the buyer is not stated. The features themselves are in the children: Companion (CM-AIA-002), BigAI (CM-AIA-003).
core: BigCommerce Companion, an AI assistant embedded directly into the control panel to help manage the business (BC-S-0349), a product line of BigCommerce (BC-I-0517).
core: BigAI creates product descriptions with AI-powered content generation and SEO optimization (BC-S-0350), a product line of BigCommerce (BC-I-0512).

The concern map holds nothing found for an MCP server that links the merchant's own AI assistant to the store. The MCP hits are BigCommerce's Storefront MCP, which connects AI agents to storefronts to search products, manage carts and hand off to checkout (BC-S-0342, BC-S-0345): a buyer's agent, cited in CM-AIA-005. The connector hit is an app type (BC-S-0324), cited in CM-APP-001.

terms: MCP Server;Storefront MCP;Agentic checkout;Agentic Search;AI discovery;Model Context Protocol
reading: core: the platform's MCP server connects AI agents to BigCommerce storefronts to search products, manage carts and hand off to checkout (BC-S-0342), with its own API resources (BC-I-0104 to BC-I-0108), enabled by the store owner in Settings > API and MCP > MCP with the Storefront MCP toggle (BC-S-0343, BC-S-0344, BC-S-0345); the product lines Agentic checkout, which keeps the merchant merchant of record (BC-S-0347, BC-I-0515), and AI discovery (BC-I-0514). extension-point, a reading: the agents are outside ones that connect through the MCP server (BC-S-0342). Agentic Search processes catalog data only, and the customer may opt out of individual platforms (BC-S-0348, BC-S-0346): shows. Which AI platforms receive the catalog is not named.

core: the Admin API, GraphQL, to query and mutate store data server-side (BC-S-0296, BC-I-0110), at POST /stores/{store_hash}/graphql (BC-S-0297); the product line Open APIs (BC-I-0533). The API Terms (BC-I-0461) bind its users: shows. Q1's gap on BC-C-054/decides (searched, not found): no statement says who enables the Admin API or on which plans.

core: three types of OAuth-based API accounts, store-level, app-level and account-level credentials (BC-S-0302); the platform's two app types, single-click and connector, defined by the method of authentication (BC-S-0324); once granted, a single-click app requests a permanent access_token to call the REST API on the user's behalf (BC-S-0330).

core: store-level access tokens and OAuth scopes can't be changed (BC-S-0304); a default scope is automatically accessible to all API accounts (BC-S-0306); the scope store_app_extensions_manage requires an app-level API account (BC-S-0328). The best practice to limit each account's scope to what it needs (BC-S-0307) is a reason: shows. The account-level scopes are cited in CM-API-013. Scopes placed in other domains' concerns (such as store_v2_orders_read_only) are not cited here.

shows, a reading: the API Terms bind the API client to protect information collected from Your Users through it from unauthorized access, use or disclosure (BC-S-0305). No statement shows the platform approving an app's access to buyers' data, or a scope or level for it.

core: apps using OAuth are rate-limited on a quota refreshed every 30 seconds (BC-S-0308), shared by all apps accessing the store (BC-S-0314), its maximum varying by store plan and requested resources (BC-S-0312): Pro 60k per hour, Plus and Standard 20k per hour (BC-S-0309, BC-S-0310), and an Unlimited Rate Plan with no limits for some Enterprise clients (BC-S-0311). The API Terms' volume limits (BC-S-0313), the guidance on HTTP 429 (BC-S-0315) and the reason (BC-S-0316): shows.

shows, a reading: versions appear only in names, Webhooks v3 (BC-I-0076), and in endpoints marked deprecated beside their modern counterparts (BC-S-0027, a statement of BC-C-003, domain B, cited because no statement of domain F shows a version). The concern map holds no BigCommerce statement of how it versions its API or keeps a change log.

The concern map holds nothing found for an API operating on a store's data in bulk. The hits are bulk pricing rules of the Catalog API (BC-S-0017, BC-S-0026), a store metafields endpoint (BC-S-0276) and a B2B webhook topic (BC-S-0358), none of them bulk operations.

core: Webhooks v3 (BC-I-0076), to get notified when specific events occur on a store (BC-S-0317), delivered to several endpoint types (BC-S-0321), in the default scope of every API account (BC-S-0306). The platform deactivates a webhook after its final retry, 48 hours on, and emails the app (BC-S-0318), blocklists a destination below a 90% success ratio for three minutes (BC-S-0319), sends store/hook/deliveryException to another destination when deliveries fail (BC-S-0320, BC-I-0153), and deletes an app's webhooks on uninstall (BC-S-0323). The reason for its limits (BC-S-0322): shows.

The concern map holds nothing found for webhooks a merchant sets up in the control panel. Its statements show webhooks registered and configured by the API client (BC-S-0320, BC-S-0306), cited in CM-API-008.
The concern map holds nothing found for webhooks with conditions. The hits are promotions' conditions (BC-S-0055), a PCI condition (BC-S-0166) and search filters (BC-S-0066), none about webhooks.

The concern map holds nothing found for webhook topics passing data subject requests to apps. The hits are the merchant's responsibility for privacy laws on the storefront (BC-S-0217) and certifications (BC-S-0421), of domain A.
The concern map holds nothing found for caching the API's responses. The hits are the shipping-quote cache (BC-S-0382, domain C) and Cloudflare's CDN (BC-S-0448, domain A).

core: the Account API manages account-level resources such as users (BC-S-0299); its users feature creates, edits and deletes control panel users (BC-S-0298); account-level credentials reach all the account's stores, not only the one signed in at creation (BC-S-0301); its API resources (BC-I-0109, BC-I-0103) and its scopes account_read, account_apps_read, account_stores_read, account_subscriptions_read and _cancel, account_users_read, _write and _delete (BC-S-0300, BC-I-0369 to BC-I-0377). The Unified Billing GraphQL API uses account-level tokens (BC-S-0181): shows.

core: the platform's two app types, single-click and connector (BC-S-0324); the scope for App Extensions (BC-S-0328, BC-I-0321); the product line Integrations (BC-I-0537). extension-point: a Third-Party Product installed or enabled for use with the Service, whose provider the merchant lets access its data (BC-S-0327). The Master Services Agreement (BC-I-0456) leaves Third-Party Products to their own terms (BC-S-0460); Commerce may disable them at any time or stop supporting an integration (BC-S-0462, BC-S-0461); dealings with their providers are between the merchant and them (BC-S-0463): shows. What App Extensions extend is not stated.

core: the BigCommerce App Marketplace, through which merchants buy apps (BC-S-0172), whose Marketplace team reviews and tests all app submissions against its listing standards (BC-S-0325). extension-point: its 21 categories, from Accounting & Tax to Site Tools (BC-I-0476 to BC-I-0496).

terms: Unified Billing;Unified Billing Partner;Unified Billing badge;Unified Billing Terms
reading: core: Unified Billing puts app charges on the merchant's BigCommerce invoice (BC-S-0172, BC-S-0183); the merchant opts in by buying from a Unified Billing Partner (BC-S-0173); Commerce collects and disburses the monies as the partners' agent (BC-S-0175, BC-S-0179; US, UK and Canada), and in India collects through its payment processor and invoices the merchant (BC-S-0177, BC-S-0178); the Unified Billing GraphQL API and its scope account_checkouts_create (BC-S-0181, BC-S-0180). outside: third-party payment processors handle all payments (BC-S-0182). shows: the partner's condition (BC-S-0174), the effect of payment to Commerce (BC-S-0176), the Unified Billing Terms (BC-I-0469 to BC-I-0471). No statement says Commerce keeps a share of the charge.

core: the webhook topic store/app/uninstalled, fired when a client store is cancelled and uninstalled from the platform (BC-S-0329, BC-I-0210). No topic for install, authorization or subscription changes is held.

The concern map holds nothing found for app-written functions the platform hosts. The hits are a multi-storefront reason (BC-S-0230) and subprocessors' names (BC-S-0446, BC-I-0554, BC-I-0556). Provider APIs, where BigCommerce calls the app's own endpoints (BC-S-0395, domain C), are not hosted by the platform (notes.md).

The concern map holds nothing found for an app's pages or extensions inside the control panel. The hits are Embedded Payment Providers (domain C), Companion embedded in the control panel (BC-S-0349, cited in CM-AIA-002) and the scope for App Extensions (BC-S-0328), whose statement doesn't say what they extend; cited in CM-APP-001.
The concern map holds nothing found for an app's page shown inside the control panel; the hits are those of CM-APP-006.

The concern map holds nothing found for an app's blocks, actions or links on the control panel's pages. App Extensions has a scope (BC-S-0328, BC-I-0321), but no statement says what they extend, so it is cited in CM-APP-001; checkout extensions (BC-S-0100, BC-S-0101) are of domain C.

core: merchants generate single-store API credentials when they create API accounts in Settings > Store-level API accounts (BC-S-0303). extension-point, a reading: only approved partners can create unlisted apps (BC-S-0326); that an unlisted app is not listed in the App Marketplace is a reading of its name.
The concern map holds nothing found for parameters an app defines and the platform holds per store. The Settings API hits are the store's own settings (BC-S-0263, domain A).

own-service: Commerce.com US, Inc., and in other jurisdictions Commerce.com Pty. Ltd., contract for the Ecommerce Platform, Extensions and certain Professional Services (BC-S-0428, BC-S-0432; statements of BC-C-079, domain A, cited as maker evidence). An Extension is a Service, not a Third-Party Product (BC-S-0464): shows. No statement shows Extensions in a category of their own in the App Marketplace, or says what they are.
The concern map holds nothing found for linking the store to a marketplace account for extensions. The hit is the connection to Amazon, eBay and Walmart (BC-S-0369, domain E), a sales channel.

The concern map holds nothing found for automations the merchant builds from triggers and actions. The hits are returns and B2B workflows (BC-S-0117, BC-S-0194), a webhook's trigger fields (BC-S-0269), Provider APIs' data flow (BC-S-0395) and ShipperHQ's shipping rules engine (BC-I-0410).

The concern map holds nothing found that describes BigCommerce's developer tools or documentation as such. Its statements are drawn from pages under /developer/ (their identifiers), and Stencil and Catalyst are storefront frameworks (BC-S-0238, BC-S-0281, domain E).
The concern map holds nothing found for a command-line tool; the CLI hits are inside other words (client).

The concern map holds nothing found for stores a partner keeps to build on or prepare. Powered By's Create Store (BC-S-0359) creates the partner's merchants' stores, cited in CM-PTN-010; StagingPro's sandbox (BC-S-0414) is cited in CM-DVT-006.
The concern map holds nothing found for free stores given to developers. The one hit, StagingPro's sandbox for Enterprise-level stores (BC-S-0414), stages a store's own changes; cited in CM-DVT-006.
The concern map holds nothing found.

core: Staging environments, a product line (BC-I-0540), to test, preview and deploy updates without disrupting live storefronts (BC-S-0413); StagingPro, a sandbox, testing, staging and CI/CD solution for Enterprise-level stores, added through the BigCommerce representative (BC-S-0414, BC-S-0415). StagingPro uses Git, BigCommerce's APIs and its own public API (BC-S-0416): shows. No statement names StagingPro's maker; placed core by what the statements show (gap in notes.md).

core: the Partner Portal, where a partner holds an account with approved Partner status (BC-S-0174). shows: the Merchant-Client Terms (BC-I-0465) for those who use the Services as a client's agent (BC-S-0474), binding the client (BC-S-0476), confirming the relationship in writing (BC-S-0477), with notices to agent or client at Commerce's discretion (BC-S-0475). No statement names a partner programme or its terms as such.
core: a Partner Portal Account with approved Partner status (BC-S-0174). Only approved partners can create unlisted apps (BC-S-0326): shows. No statement shows how a partner is approved.

core, a reading: Commerce collects and disburses monies in the Unified Billing Partners' name as their agent (BC-S-0179, BC-S-0175), so the partners are paid through the platform. outside: third-party payment processors handle the payments (BC-S-0182). No statement shows a payout schedule, a share or holds.
The concern map holds nothing found for the platform invoicing partners. The invoice hits are Unified Billing's merchant invoice (CM-APP-003) and B2B invoices (domain C).

The concern map holds nothing found for a directory or marketplace of partners' services. The hits are Commerce's own Professional Services (BC-S-0428, BC-S-0432), cited in CM-APP-011 as maker evidence.
The concern map holds nothing found; the hits are plan names and payment terms.

The concern map holds nothing found for a programme connecting partners with merchants expanding abroad. The hits are Agentic checkout's merchant of record (BC-S-0347, in CM-AIA-005) and the Tax Settings API (BC-S-0387, domain C).
The concern map holds nothing found for a referral programme; the hits are the MSA's parties (BC-S-0425) and the European Commission (BC-S-0453).
The concern map holds nothing found; the one affiliate hit is the MSA's parties (BC-S-0425).

core: Powered By, to resell ecommerce with Commerce-as-a-Service (BC-S-0360), with its API group Beta Powered By > Stores and > Plans (BC-S-0359, BC-S-0363, BC-I-0115). extension-point: its partner-focused APIs let partners offer BigCommerce stores to their merchants and onboard them (BC-S-0361), and the partner may own the billing relationship or let BigCommerce bill the merchant (BC-S-0362). It is a closed beta, by request to support (BC-S-0077): shows.
